title: An internal stinger. A more compact direction.
summary: The selected exhaust direction retains an internal stinger in a completely straight system, with no bends inside the hull. This updated record preserves the earlier sketch, provisional dimensions and the engine alignment and fit checks still required.
dateLabel: 10 Oct 2026 · internal-stinger concept and routing decision
heroAlt: Section-only detail of the internal stinger extending upstream through the baffle into the belly; the superseded bend plan is excluded.
heroCaption: Internal-stinger section detail from the earlier sketch. It illustrates the tube arrangement, not a validated straight-system CAD revision. Dimensions remain provisional; the baffle junction needs redesign.
thumbnailAlt: Section of the selected internal-stinger concept, extending upstream through the baffle into the belly.

sections.title: Keep the length, bring the tube inside
sections.text: The latest study carries the stinger through the baffle and extends its inlet upstream into the belly. Instead of adding the entire outlet tube beyond the chamber, the two overlap physically. This is a packaging concept for the compact installation, not a demonstrated power improvement.

sections.title: What the sketch actually specifies
sections.text: The supplied drawing shows an 18 mm internal-diameter stinger, 215 mm total tube length, 195 mm inside the chamber and 20 mm projecting outside. Its inlet lies approximately 33 mm upstream of the baffle, within the belly. These are the variant’s sketch dimensions; the earlier Rev01 reference uses a 216 mm external stinger. The 1 mm difference is retained explicitly rather than silently changing either record.

sections.title: Current requirement: a completely straight system
sections.text: The founder’s latest instruction supersedes the sideways-exit and R50 turn: there is no space for bends or turns inside the hull. Keep the internal stinger, but develop a straight exhaust system. The engine exhaust-port and flange orientation must accommodate the straight installation; their alignment and actual hull clearances are not yet verified. No bend should be introduced to make the earlier layout fit.

sections.title: The baffle junction needs redesign
sections.text: An 18 mm internal-diameter tube with an assumed 1 mm radial wall has a 20 mm outside diameter. It cannot pass through the earlier 18 mm opening without revising the junction. The baffle termination, tube support, sealing and thermal movement need their own geometry and engineering checks. The illustration describes the concept; it does not resolve these interfaces.

sections.title: Why the inlet position matters
sections.text: Gordon Jennings describes historical internal-outlet experiments in the Two-Stroke Tuner’s Handbook, pp. 69–71. His account supports investigating an inlet ahead of the baffle and reports adverse behaviour with an inlet near its midpoint. Those tests concerned other engines. They do not establish Wahoo power, noise, temperature or the correct inlet position for this engine.

sections.title: Packaging and tuning are separate questions
sections.text: Bringing the stinger inside does not simply subtract its length from the acoustic system. The chamber now discharges at a different internal location, and the tube occupies part of its volume. The earlier 575 mm effective-length assumption cannot establish unchanged tuning. Exhaust and transfer port data, operating speed, temperatures and pressure histories must inform the next gas-dynamic study.

sections.title: Cooling, service access and the installed hull
sections.text: The water jacket remains a development requirement, with exhaust gas separated from jacket water. Support, welds, jacket sealing, drainage, cooling supply and outlet backflow protection remain unresolved. The compact direction must still leave access for servicing and assembly removal through the hatch. Neither the schematic board outline nor the shortened projection proves hull fit or service clearance.

sections.title: Decision and next steps
sections.text: Decision EXH-002, updated: carry forward the internal stinger in a completely straight exhaust, with no bends or turns inside the hull. This supersedes the earlier sideways-exit/R50 routing concept. All dimensions remain provisional until the engine data is established. Retain WHE-EXH-001 Rev01 as the external-stinger comparison. Next, align the engine outlet with the straight installation, resolve the tube/baffle interface and cooling detail, check the actual internal hull and removal paths, and compare the variants through engine-linked analysis and controlled measurements.

sections.title: Reference CAD and the superseded routing sketch
sections.text: The supplied wahoo_exhaust_section.dxf and wahoo_exhaust_provisional.step have been retained in the engineering archive as provisional millimetre references. The STEP identifies exhaust pipe, internal stinger and water jacket components. Their geometry has not been validated, and they do not establish compliance with the latest straight-system requirement. The earlier drawing below is retained only as development history: its R50 bend and 617 mm aft-projection label are superseded, not current installation specifications.

changes: Adds the internal-stinger variant and decision EXH-002 without replacing the external-stinger reference. Website graphics preserve supplied coordinates; metadata and fixed light-theme styles are removed for display. No native CAD, raw simulation or private source package is published. Straight-routing update: latest founder instruction supersedes the R50 bend. The hero and thumbnail now show only the internal-stinger section. Earlier plan retained as explicitly superseded history; no duplicate investigation created.
